options.a: Lets the lender demand full payoff if the property is sold
options.b: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early
options.c: Lets the lender accelerate the full balance after a borrower default
options.d: Charges a fee when the borrower's monthly payment arrives late

distractorExplanations.a: That is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, which is triggered by a transfer rather than an early payoff.
distractorExplanations.c: That is an acceleration clause, which is triggered by default rather than by voluntary early payoff.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a late-payment charge; a prepayment penalty applies when the borrower pays early, not late.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. The penalty applies only when the note and law allow it.

options.a: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.b: Finance construction draws as a new home is built, then convert to a permanent loan
options.c: Combine a first and second mortgage to avoid PMI on an 80/10/10 purchase
options.d: Let a buyer take over the seller's existing loan on its original terms

distractorExplanations.b: That describes a construction (construction-to-permanent) loan, which funds building rather than a sale gap.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a piggyback loan structure used to avoid PMI, not short-term gap financing between homes.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a loan assumption, where the buyer takes over the seller's mortgage, not a bridge loan.

options.a: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.b: Practicing law whenever they complete any blank on a standard purchase form
options.c: Acting as the escrow agent and must hold the earnest money until closing
options.d: Required to have the buyer's attorney approve each blank before signing

distractorExplanations.b: Filling blanks on approved forms is generally permitted; it becomes law practice when drafting new legal clauses.
distractorExplanations.c: Completing a form does not make the licensee an escrow agent; who holds earnest money is set by the contract.
distractorExplanations.d: Attorney review may be recommended, but there is no general rule requiring attorney approval of each blank.

options.a: 1% of the purchase price
options.b: 1% of the loan amount
options.c: 1% of the down payment
options.d: 1% of the interest rate

distractorExplanations.a: Points are based on the loan amount, not the price; with a down payment the loan is smaller than the price.
distractorExplanations.c: The down payment is the buyer's equity, not the base for points; points are 1% of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.d: A point is a fee on the loan amount; it may buy down the rate but is not computed from the rate.

options.a: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.b: Interest each month, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.c: Principal only, with interest added to the balance each month
options.d: Interest and principal in payments that increase each year of the term

distractorExplanations.b: That describes an interest-only or straight term loan with a balloon, not a fully amortizing loan.
distractorExplanations.c: Adding unpaid interest to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of an amortizing payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Rising payments describe a graduated payment mortgage; a fixed-rate amortizing payment stays level.

options.a: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.b: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.c: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.b: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: Disclosure of the APR and finance charges to consumer borrowers
options.b: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.c: Lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.d: Fees for referring settlement services in residential loans

distractorExplanations.a: Credit cost disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act; usury laws cap the rate itself.
distractorExplanations.c: Credit discrimination is governed by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, not usury laws.
distractorExplanations.d: Referral fees and kickbacks for settlement services are restricted by RESPA, not usury laws.

options.a: The seller's reasons for selling and the lowest price the seller is willing to accept
options.b: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood surrounding the property
options.c: That a former occupant of the home was living with HIV or AIDS
options.d: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts.
distractorExplanations.b: Discussing neighborhood racial or religious composition is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required disclosure.
distractorExplanations.c: HIV/AIDS is a protected disability under federal fair housing law; it is not a material property fact to disclose.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared; confidential motivations may be protected. Disclosure duties follow applicable law.

options.a: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
options.b: Can adjust whenever the lender chooses, without caps
options.c: Adjusts with the margin while the index stays fixed
options.d: Changes only when the borrower refinances the loan

distractorExplanations.b: ARM changes follow a published index on set adjustment dates, and periodic and lifetime caps limit each change.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the terms: the margin is fixed for the loan's life, and the index is the variable part that moves.
distractorExplanations.d: A refinance replaces the loan with a new note; an ARM's rate resets on scheduled adjustment dates under the existing note.

options.a: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.b: Parties may still perform within a reasonable time after each stated deadline passes
options.c: The closing date is firm, but other contingency deadlines may slip
options.d: The offer expires if the seller does not accept it within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.b: That is the default rule when the clause is absent; time is of the essence makes the stated deadlines strictly enforceable.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause applies to all contract dates, including inspection, financing, and appraisal contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the clause with an offer's expiration term; time is of the essence governs performance deadlines in the contract.

options.a: Must acquire title at the same time and by the same deed as each other
options.b: Hold equal undivided shares, and a deceased owner's share passes to the others
options.c: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.d: Cannot sell or will their share without the other co-owners' consent

distractorExplanations.a: Unity of time and title are joint tenancy requirements; tenants in common may acquire their shares at different times by different deeds.
distractorExplanations.b: Equal shares plus right of survivorship are joint tenancy features; a tenant in common's share passes to heirs or devisees.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may freely sell, mortgage, or will an undivided share without the other co-owners' consent.

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term
options.d: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.c: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: The broker's compensation is a fixed percentage of the final sale price
options.b: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.c: The seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission
options.d: The broker's flat fee is owed up front even if the property does not sell

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a standard percentage commission listing, which does not create the net listing's incentive to underprice.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an exclusive agency listing, not a net listing where the broker keeps everything above the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a net listing with a flat-fee or advance-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker only the excess over the net price.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings pay the broker the amount above the seller's net price, creating conflict-of-interest concerns: they can incentivize underpricing and are banned or tightly regulated in many places.

options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms within a period, once consideration is paid
options.b: A right of first refusal to match any offer the owner later accepts
options.c: An equitable title that passes legal title once payments are complete
options.d: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration

distractorExplanations.a: Only the optionor (owner) is bound; the optionee holds a right, not an obligation, to buy, making the option unilateral.
distractorExplanations.b: A right of first refusal only lets the holder match a third-party offer; an option fixes the price and terms in advance.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a vendee's position under a land contract (contract for deed), not an optionee's unexercised right.

options.a: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures
options.b: Requiring APR and finance charge disclosures for all consumer credit
options.c: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.d: Requiring lenders to report loan data by census tract to regulators

distractorExplanations.b: APR and finance-charge disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA's settlement-services focus.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA); RESPA targets settlement kickbacks and closing-cost disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Census-tract loan reporting is the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA), which tracks lending patterns, not settlement costs.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures in covered transactions (with TRID integration for many loans).

options.a: The seller owes no commission if the seller personally finds the buyer, but owes it if any broker does
options.b: Whichever broker first produces a ready, willing, and able buyer earns the fee, and the listing then ends
options.c: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.d: The listing broker keeps any sale proceeds above the seller's stated net price as the commission

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the owner keeps the right to sell commission-free; exclusive right-to-sell removes that exception.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes an open listing given to several brokers; an exclusive right-to-sell names one listing broker for the whole term.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, a separate (and widely discouraged) arrangement, not the exclusive right-to-sell commission trigger.

options.a: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.b: Suggest an offer price, since customers are owed the same advice as clients
options.c: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can make a strong offer
options.d: Give the buyer pricing advice as long as the seller is told about it after closing

distractorExplanations.b: Customers are owed honesty and disclosure of material facts, not advice; advising on price is advocacy reserved for clients.
distractorExplanations.c: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality duty the listing agent owes the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure after closing is too late; any shift toward representing the buyer needs informed consent before the advice is given.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If the buyer wants advice, the broker must properly create buyer agency (with the required disclosures and consents) where the law allows.

options.a: Later regrets agreeing to a price that was too high
options.b: Was induced by fraud or was a minor
options.c: Agreed orally to a lease of one year or less
options.d: Was declared legally incompetent before signing

distractorExplanations.a: Buyer's remorse over price is not a legal ground; a contract freely made by a competent, informed party is valid and enforceable.
distractorExplanations.c: Oral leases of one year or less are generally enforceable under the statute of frauds; this confuses them with longer leases that must be written.
distractorExplanations.d: A contract signed by someone already adjudicated incompetent is generally void, not voidable; this confuses void with voidable.

options.a: A seller's written warranty that the home's systems will stay defect-free after closing
options.b: A credit-terms claim regulated under the Truth in Lending Act advertising rules
options.c: Negligent misrepresentation of a material fact that the licensee should have verified
options.d: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty

distractorExplanations.a: A written promise about condition is an express warranty that can be enforced, the opposite of non-binding opinion puffing.
distractorExplanations.b: TILA/Regulation Z governs advertised financing terms such as APR and payments, not subjective sales opinions like "stunning views".
distractorExplanations.c: A misstated measurable fact (size, age, room count) is misrepresentation, which creates liability; puffing is limited to opinion.

options.a: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.b: Proceed as a dual agent if the buyer consents in writing, since one party's consent is enough
options.c: Proceed with the dual agency and obtain the seller's signed consent at or after closing
options.d: Represent both parties anyway but withhold the seller's confidential pricing information

distractorExplanations.b: Dual agency needs informed written consent from both clients; the buyer's consent alone cannot override the seller's refusal.
distractorExplanations.c: Consent must be informed and given before dual agency begins; collecting it at closing makes it an undisclosed dual agency.
distractorExplanations.d: Keeping confidences does not cure the problem; acting for both sides without the seller's consent is still undisclosed dual agency.

options.a: Disbursing funds per a written release agreement
options.b: Using client trust money to pay brokerage expenses
options.c: Holding funds for several clients in one trust account
options.d: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds

distractorExplanations.b: Spending trust money on the firm's own bills is conversion, a separate and more serious violation than mixing the funds.
distractorExplanations.c: A single pooled trust account for many clients is permitted when each client has its own ledger; it is not commingling.
distractorExplanations.a: Proper disbursement is compliance.

options.a: Curtesy
options.b: Devise by will
options.c: Survivorship
options.d: Homestead

distractorExplanations.a: Curtesy is a husband's marital interest in a deceased wife's land, a marital-rights concept unrelated to joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.b: A joint tenant cannot pass the interest by will; on death it passes to the surviving joint tenants, which defeats any devise.
distractorExplanations.d: Homestead protects a residence from certain creditors and is a separate statutory right, not a feature of joint tenancy.

options.a: Public use and the owner's written consent
options.b: Public use/purpose and just compensation
options.c: Public purpose and payment at tax-assessed value
options.d: Owner tax default followed by a public sale

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is an involuntary taking; the owner's consent is not required, which is why condemnation proceedings exist.
distractorExplanations.c: Just compensation is measured by fair market value, not the tax-assessed value, which often differs from market value.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a tax sale for unpaid property taxes, an enforcement remedy, not the government's power of eminent domain.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. The Fifth Amendment Takings Clause is the constitutional framework.

options.a: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.b: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.c: When the life tenant sells the interest
options.d: After 99 years, like a long-term ground lease

distractorExplanations.b: The remainderman holds the future interest; his death does not end the life estate, which is measured by the life tenant or named life.
distractorExplanations.c: A life tenant may convey the interest, but the buyer then holds an estate pur autre vie that still ends at the measuring life's death.
distractorExplanations.d: A fixed 99-year term describes a leasehold or ground lease; a life estate is measured by a human life, not a set number of years.

options.a: A zoning restriction that limits how the owner may use the land
options.b: A title insurance commitment listing the policy's coverage terms
options.c: A survey showing the property's boundaries and improvements
options.d: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability

distractorExplanations.a: Zoning is a public land-use regulation under police power, not a private claim or defect casting doubt on who owns the title.
distractorExplanations.b: A title commitment is the insurer's offer to insure; it may list clouds as exceptions but is not itself a cloud on title.
distractorExplanations.c: A survey documents boundaries and improvements; it can reveal an encroachment, but the survey itself is not a title cloud.

options.a: Approval of a special use the ordinance permits if listed conditions are met
options.b: Permanent change of the zoning map for an entire district
options.c: The right to continue a use that predates the current zoning law
options.d: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a conditional (special) use permit, which allows a listed use, not hardship relief from a zoning requirement.
distractorExplanations.c: That is a legal nonconforming (grandfathered) use, which arises from prior use, not from a hardship application.
distractorExplanations.b: That is rezoning/amendment.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. It is granted by the zoning authority, typically a board of zoning appeals.

options.a: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.b: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.c: Having the deed notarized by a licensed notary
options.d: Sending a copy to the county tax assessor's office

distractorExplanations.b: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties, but they give no notice to the world until the deed is recorded.
distractorExplanations.c: Acknowledgment before a notary makes a deed eligible for recording; it does not itself give constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.d: The assessor's office keeps tax rolls, not the public land records; constructive notice comes from recording with the recorder/register of deeds.

options.a: Land bordering a navigable lake, sea, or ocean shoreline
options.b: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.c: Rights to divert water under the prior appropriation system
options.d: Rights to minerals and other resources below the land surface

distractorExplanations.a: Rights of owners along lakes, seas, and oceans are littoral rights; riparian rights concern flowing rivers and streams.
distractorExplanations.c: Prior appropriation ("first in time, first in right") is a competing western water doctrine, not the riparian doctrine.
distractorExplanations.d: Subsurface mineral rights are a separate bundle of rights that can be severed; they are unrelated to water-boundary rights.

options.a: Title defects first created after the policy's effective date
options.b: Covered title defects and claims against ownership
options.c: Lender losses when the borrower defaults on the loan
options.d: Physical damage to the structure from fire or storms

distractorExplanations.a: Title insurance covers defects existing as of the policy date; matters arising afterward are not covered.
distractorExplanations.c: Losses from borrower default are covered by mortgage insurance (PMI, FHA MIP), not by title insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: Physical damage is a hazard or homeowner's insurance risk; title insurance covers ownership defects, not casualty.

options.a: The seller is charged; it reduces the seller's proceeds
options.b: The item is prorated and split evenly between both parties
options.c: The buyer receives a credit reducing cash to close
options.d: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed

distractorExplanations.a: A debit falls on the party in whose column it appears; a buyer debit charges the buyer, not the seller.
distractorExplanations.b: Proration divides an item by days of ownership and produces offsetting entries; it does not define what a buyer debit means.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a credit.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. A seller debit likewise reduces the seller's proceeds.

options.a: Originate and fund new loans directly to borrowers at the closing table
options.b: Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV loans
options.c: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators
options.d: Set the federal funds rate that drives mortgage pricing

distractorExplanations.a: Making and funding loans to borrowers is the primary mortgage market; the secondary market buys loans already made.
distractorExplanations.b: Default protection on high loan-to-value loans is the role of private mortgage insurance or FHA, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.d: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target rate; Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy loans but do not set that rate.

options.a: Retained by the broker as compensation for the cost of maintaining the trust account
options.b: Added to the commission split between the listing and cooperating brokers at closing
options.c: According to statutory rules (e.g., client benefit or approved housing-trust programs)
options.d: Swept into the brokerage operating account monthly and reported as business income

distractorExplanations.a: Trust interest belongs to whoever the law or the parties' written agreement designates; the broker cannot keep it as a fee by default.
distractorExplanations.b: Interest on client money is not part of brokerage compensation; adding it to the commission split converts trust funds.
distractorExplanations.d: Moving trust interest into operating funds is commingling/conversion; it must stay in trust until disbursed as the rules direct.

options.a: Replaces the need for written listing and buyer agency agreements with clients
options.b: Shifts responsibility for associates' violations from the broker to the associates
options.c: Documents supervision standards and compliant procedures for affiliated licensees
options.d: Satisfies the associates' continuing education requirement when reviewed annually

distractorExplanations.a: A manual governs internal procedure; client agency relationships still require their own written agreements.
distractorExplanations.b: A written manual supports, but does not transfer, the broker's statutory duty to supervise affiliated licensees.
distractorExplanations.d: Reading an office manual is not approved continuing education; CE must come from approved courses and providers.

options.a: Pay the rebate personally to the buyer without routing it through the broker
options.b: Refuse, because commission rebates to buyers are banned under federal RESPA
options.c: Pay the rebate out of the earnest money deposit held in the trust account
options.d: Follow brokerage rules on rebates and ensure any payment is lawful and disclosed

distractorExplanations.a: Licensees must handle compensation through their employing broker; a private side payment bypasses the broker and disclosure.
distractorExplanations.b: RESPA Section 8 targets kickbacks between settlement providers; it does not prohibit a disclosed rebate to the consumer.
distractorExplanations.c: Earnest money belongs to the parties under the contract; using it to fund a rebate is misuse of trust funds.

options.a: Perform licensed activities under the associate's license, since the associate supervises them
options.b: Perform licensed activities only within their own license authority and brokerage affiliation rules
options.c: Accept payment for licensed work directly from the associate who hired them
options.d: Hold client earnest money in the associate's account until closing

distractorExplanations.a: A licensee acts under their own license and the employing broker's supervision; an associate cannot lend their license authority.
distractorExplanations.c: Compensation for licensed activity must come through the employing broker, not directly from another associate.
distractorExplanations.d: Client funds must go into the broker's designated trust account; neither the assistant nor the associate may hold them.

options.a: Protect confidential client information and not disclose without authority or legal requirement
options.b: Disclose it, because fiduciary duties to the seller end once the transaction has closed
options.c: Refer the buyer to the title company, which may release closing addresses to any party
options.d: Disclose it if the buyer signs a written release of liability for the listing agent

distractorExplanations.b: The duty of confidentiality survives closing for non-public personal information; other duties ending does not lift it.
distractorExplanations.c: Routing the request through a third party is still an unauthorized disclosure; title companies do not owe the buyer the seller's address.
distractorExplanations.d: A release from the buyer cannot authorize disclosure; only the seller client or a legal requirement can.

options.a: Deposited into a properly designated trust/escrow account within required timelines
options.b: Deposited into the broker's operating account and moved to trust before closing
options.c: Held uncashed in the transaction file until all contingencies are removed
options.d: Deposited into the associate licensee's own escrow account within two days

distractorExplanations.b: Placing client money in the operating account, even briefly, is commingling; it must go straight into the trust account.
distractorExplanations.c: Deposit deadlines run from receipt or acceptance, not from contingency removal; holding the check past the deadline is a violation.
distractorExplanations.d: Trust funds belong in the employing broker's designated trust account; associates may not hold their own escrow accounts.

options.a: Start working for the new broker at once and file the transfer at next renewal
options.b: Reapply as a new licensee and retake the state portion of the license exam
options.c: Follow transfer procedures so the license is properly affiliated
options.d: Wait until the old broker's pending deals close before filing

distractorExplanations.a: Affiliation must be updated when the move happens; practicing for the new broker before transfer is unlicensed activity for that firm.
distractorExplanations.b: Changing brokers is a transfer of an existing license; it does not require a new application or re-examination.
distractorExplanations.d: No such waiting period applies; pending deals stay with the old firm, but the transfer can be filed right away.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-mi-licens.explanation: Affiliation changes require regulatory notice/transfer steps. The transfer is filed with LARA; the licensee may not act for the new broker until it is processed.

options.a: Keeping records until the listing agreement expires
options.b: Keeping transaction records for one year after closing, then shredding
options.c: Keeping only trust account records; other files may be discarded at closing
options.d: Keeping transaction records for the required period

distractorExplanations.a: Retention runs for a set period after closing (or the final transaction event), not just until the listing term ends.
distractorExplanations.b: One year is shorter than the state retention period; destroying files that early violates recordkeeping rules.
distractorExplanations.c: Retention rules cover the full transaction file (agreements, disclosures, offers), not just trust account records.

mi-real-estate-readiness-check-mi-licens.explanation: Statutory retention periods protect consumers and enable audits. The minimum retention period is set by LARA rules.

options.a: Acceptable if the promise is put in writing and signed by the licensee
options.b: Permitted puffing, since predictions about future value are opinions
options.c: Generally improper/misleading and can be a license law violation
options.d: A violation only if the buyer later suffers a measurable loss

distractorExplanations.a: Putting a misleading guarantee in writing does not cure it; it creates written evidence of a deceptive assurance.
distractorExplanations.b: A direct promise of profit is a specific assurance a buyer may rely on, not vague opinion; it falls outside puffing.
distractorExplanations.d: The misleading promise itself can be the violation; discipline does not wait for the buyer to lose money.

options.a: Promptly as required by agency and license rules
options.b: Only after the buyer's lender issues a written preapproval
options.c: Within the 72-hour review window set in the listing agreement
options.d: After the seller has responded to every earlier offer received

distractorExplanations.b: Financing strength is for the seller to weigh; the agent may not hold back an offer until a preapproval arrives.
distractorExplanations.c: No fixed review window replaces the duty to present promptly; delaying an offer by days can cost the seller the buyer.
distractorExplanations.d: Offers must be presented as they arrive, including while another offer is pending, unless the seller lawfully waives this.

options.a: Transfers to the departing associate, who becomes the records custodian
options.b: Remains with the brokerage; the firm retains responsibility for records
options.c: Goes with the clients, who may take the original file to their next agent
options.d: Is split so the associate keeps open listings and the broker keeps closed files

distractorExplanations.a: Transaction records belong to the broker, who stays responsible for keeping them; the departing associate does not take custody.
distractorExplanations.c: Clients may receive copies of their documents, but the brokerage must keep the original records for the retention period.
distractorExplanations.d: Listings are contracts with the brokerage, not the associate; open listings and their files stay with the firm.

options.a: They let the broker withdraw earned interest as operating income
options.b: They replace the need for separate ledgers for each client or transaction
options.c: They are needed only when the regulator schedules an audit
options.d: They help detect shortages/overages and demonstrate compliance

distractorExplanations.a: Reconciliation verifies balances; it does not authorize the broker to take trust interest, which follows the trust rules.
distractorExplanations.b: Reconciliation compares the bank statement, journal, and individual client ledgers; it depends on those ledgers rather than replacing them.
distractorExplanations.c: Reconciliation is a regular (typically monthly) duty, not an audit-time task; shortages must be caught as they happen.

options.a: Decline to respond until the complainant files a civil lawsuit
options.b: Respond only through the broker, since associates cannot answer
options.c: Cooperate as required and respond truthfully within deadlines
options.d: Settle privately with the complainant so the regulator must close it

distractorExplanations.a: A regulatory investigation runs separately from civil suits; failing to respond by the deadline is itself grounds for discipline.
distractorExplanations.b: The licensee named in the complaint must respond personally; the broker may also be asked to respond but does not replace the licensee.
distractorExplanations.d: A private settlement or withdrawn complaint does not bind the regulator, which can continue the investigation to protect the public.

options.a: Illegal under federal fair housing law and typically also violates license standards
options.b: Legal if the seller gives the instruction in writing and the agent documents it
options.c: Allowed for single-family homes sold by owners under the federal exemption
options.d: Illegal only when the property is listed in the MLS or advertised

distractorExplanations.b: A seller's written instruction cannot authorize discrimination; following it makes the licensee liable as well as the seller.
distractorExplanations.c: The single-family owner exemption is lost once a licensee is used; a broker can never rely on it to refuse a showing.
distractorExplanations.d: Fair housing law applies to the refusal itself, whether or not the home is in the MLS or advertised publicly.
